Subject: Clarify invoicing triggers for prompt-cache hits & SKU mapping

Hi Lara —

Thanks for the earlier demo and for outlining your usage patterns. To help your procurement and finance teams, can we clarify how prefix/prompt caching shows up on the invoice? Two specific asks:

1) Billing trigger: For repeated requests that hit the prefix cache within the configured TTL, are clients invoiced for the full request token count, a reduced cache-hit SKU, or only non-cacheable tokens? We saw differing language in the rate card and wanted a single-line rule we can hand to Acme finance.

2) SKU mapping: If a single API call mixes a cached prompt prefix plus a variable user prompt, which SKU(s) will appear (e.g., prefix-cache-hit tokens vs. runtime generation tokens)? A concrete example with token math would be super helpful.

I attached a tiny sample of your projected Q4 traffic (anticipated_traffic.csv) to ground the ask. If easier, Karthik can lay out a couple of example invoices and line items.

Goal here is to make sure procurement understands potential unit cost variability before we lock a discount band and finalize the reserved capacity proposal.

Hi Lara — thanks for the clear asks. I put together the operational rule we use and an example invoice line. High level first, then a short worked example.

Operational billing rule (single line):
- We charge only for tokens that require model computation at request time. Tokens served from the prefix cache are billed under the "prefix-cache-hit" SKU at a reduced per-token rate; full-generation tokens are billed under the standard generation SKU. When a request contains both cached and uncached tokens, the invoice will show separate line items for each SKU (cache-hit vs generation).

TTL and backfill:
- Cache hits are only billed at the time they are served. When TTL expires and the next request causes a cache miss (re-compute), that request is billed as a generation for the portion of tokens that must be recomputed. We do not backfill charges for requests that were previously served from cache.

Worked example (short):
- Prompt prefix: 40 tokens (cached)
- User suffix: 160 tokens (generated on call)
- Total request: 200 tokens

Invoice line mapping: 1) prefix-cache-hit SKU — 40 tokens @ $0.00002/token => $0.0008 (reduced rate)
2) generation SKU — 160 tokens @ $0.0008/token => $0.128
3) total line items: two rows on invoice with SKUs and quantities.

Notes on rounding and billing windows: we aggregate token counts per SKU per billing period; small per-request fractions get summed before rounding.

Discounts & reserved capacity — we can attach a rate-card that maps to three tiers: On-demand, Committed, Enterprise. For Acme's projected Q4 volumes (from your CSV) here is a short starter proposal:
- Committed 6-month minimum: 12% off generation SKU, 25% off prefix-cache-hit SKU
- Enterprise annual: 18% off generation SKU, 35% off prefix-cache-hit SKU + invoice export to your GL codes

I uploaded the rate card and a sample mocked invoice to Drive here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cACME-Procurement (file: rate_card_v3.pdf, sample_invoice_acme_q4.pdf). I've also attached rate_card_v3.pdf to this thread for quick download.

If you want, we can run a 7-day invoice simulation against your sample traffic and return per-SKU spend projections. That tends to remove surprises.

1) Confirm: if a prefix is served from cache multiple times within the TTL, we will see repeated prefix-cache-hit SKU lines (aggregated) and not the full-generation SKU, correct?
2) Can you confirm whether the prefix-cache-hit SKU rate will be fixed for the life of the committed period or if it is subject to indexation/quarterly adjustments? We prefer fixed unit economics for the committed term.

If you can confirm those two points and push the mocked invoice into a PDF we can attach to the PO, we can move to approval next week.

Best,
Lara
